prompt: In which quadrant is sine positive while cosine is negative?
hint: Sine is the $y$-coordinate and cosine is the $x$-coordinate.

hints.text: Sine is the $y$-coordinate and cosine is the $x$-coordinate.
You want a place where $y > 0$ (above the $x$-axis) and $x < 0$ (left of the $y$-axis).
Up and to the left is Quadrant II.

explanation: On the unit circle, $\cos\theta$ is the $x$-coordinate and $\sin\theta$ is the $y$-coordinate.
Sine positive means the point is above the $x$-axis; cosine negative means it is left of the $y$-axis.
Up and to the left is Quadrant II.

alternativeExplanations.title: ASTC — All Students Take Calculus
steps: Going counterclockwise from Quadrant I, the mnemonic names what is positive: All, Sine, Tangent, Cosine.
The S sits in Quadrant II, meaning only Sine is positive there — so cosine (and tangent) are negative.
